en: The Ritual for the Recitation of the Kumāra-sūtra, translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Śubhakarasiṃha. [Imperial Edict] ...
The Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, if there should be women who, for the sake of their children..."
If a child wishes to cultivate this Dharma of the Youth Sūtra,
they should first observe the eight precepts on the eighth and fifteenth days of the month.
Having bathed for purification,
donned new and clean garments,
and paid homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Rising at dawn, he recited the mantra beginning with the syllable "Lan" over water eight times,
and then wrote out the *Za tongzi jing* (Sutra of Miscellaneous Disciples) within an inkstone.
Construct a circular maṇḍala facing the east.
Place fragrant flowers, lamps, light, argha water, and so forth, filling them completely upon the maṇḍala.
Afterward, transcribe this sūtra.
Practice this method in a clean room,
or by the side of a river,
or at the foot of a mountain.
If one practices this secret rite of the *Kumāra-sūtra* at a dwelling place of monks or nuns,
one should construct a circular mandala four cubits in circumference.
Next, construct the written maṇḍala.
Within the inner court, write the Great Brahmā King.
In the [surrounding] area, write the forms and images of fifteen spirits, including Candana, Gandharva, and the great ghosts and spirits.
Having performed the actions exactly as described,
at that time the Great Brahmā King addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"It is for the sake of benefiting, nourishing, and bringing peace and happiness to the children of Jambudvīpa."
I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant permission for me to proclaim the most supreme Secret Seal Dhāraṇī. That dhāraṇī is as follows:
*tadyathā | agalagani nagagani pralugre gabrai brai bura rośe nide surabhi cara cara-patani parāha aghariśani nayide nayide svāhā*. As for the characteristics of its seal:
With the concentration mudrā, pinch the water-nail (the little finger) like the shape of a flower;
this is the wisdom fist pressed against the waist.
If one uses this dhāraṇī-seal to empower those afflicted by illness and suffering,
they shall immediately attain its cessation. This dhāraṇī binds all the devas.
All great ghost-king deities, all great and minor spirits, and all classes of beings in the dark paths—
whosoever possesses compassion shall not be broken or bound.
All ghosts, spirits, and divine kings who attempt to bind [this person] shall have their heads split into seven pieces,
like the branches of an *ari* tree.
At that time, the great ghost-king Candana Gandharva,
together with fifteen great spirits and deities of the netherworld, [appeared].
They all assembled together, prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground,
and said to the Great Brahmā King:
"We have all abandoned our evil intentions."
Protect this dhāraṇī and the boy;
we pray only that the Great Brahmā King will proclaim the dhāraṇī so that all spirits and ghosts shall protect the boy.
Furthermore, in the *Kumārarakṣā-sūtra*, which eliminates evil and brings about auspiciousness, the Candana Gandharva King spoke this dhāraṇī:
Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Viśuddha sarvarāvāḥ hī hī svāhā || [Note: *Nai-ba* (內縛) refers to the joining of the water-mudrās (*śailī-mudrā*).]
This explains the mudrā and the dhāraṇī.
This mudrā and this dhāraṇī extinguish all great epidemics.
It eliminates all four hundred and four types of illness.
All spirits and deities will constantly and eternally protect this person, never leaving their side.
This mantra accomplishes all that is sought and is sacred.
I have also spoken the fifteen *dhāraṇīs* of the spirits for the benefit of all sentient beings.
I only pray that the Great Brahmā King will now speak the fifteen *dhāraṇīs* of their retinues.
He then spoke, saying:

"Namo buddhāya (1), namo dharmāya (2), namo saṃghāya. Namo Cūḍapanthaka-rājapiśāca, Khandarohī-rājapiśāca, Apasmāraka-piśāca, Mukhacūḍa-piśāca, Mañcika-piśāca, Yamika-piśāca, Kāmika-piśāca, Lepamati-piśāca, Pūtana-piśāca, Māndāravatī-piśāca, Śakunī-piśāca, Kaṇṭhapāṇini-piśāca, Mukhamanḍa-piśāca, Lambā-piśāca. Svāhā. The Great Brahmā Deva-king addressed the Buddha once more, saying:
If there are sentient beings who can receive, uphold, recite, and chant this dhāraṇī,
ten thousand evils will be extinguished and ten thousand virtues will arise;
they shall be constantly protected by all the deities of the netherworld.
May all spirits and all malevolent deities grant their compassionate protection.
At that time, Mahābrahmā and Śakra-devendra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I possess a dhāraṇī for protecting all children."
It is called the *Dhāraṇī for Longevity and Prolonging Life*.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:

*Tadyathā | buddha buddhānāmata | bodhi bodhimale śikṣaya bhasare bhadame bharadadhure dhure bhaladadhure śamane śure bharavidhe balade śramasamidhe bandha bandhi bhagani mage mani dhape sukani bharaṇi svāhā.* The Seal of the Hand-Posture (*mudrā*).
With both palms facing upward,
join the two thumbs to press against the two ring fingers;
the movement of the two index fingers back and forth constitutes this mudrā.
If one recites this dhāraṇī, forms this mudrā,
and constantly upholds the Kumārabhūta Sūtra,
one’s lifespan will be extended by thirty-eight thousand days.
This dhāraṇī can eliminate fixed karma and extend one's lifespan;
it extinguishes immeasurable evils and gives rise to immeasurable goodness,
and is able to fulfill all aspirations.
Next, the mantras for exhorting the fifteen spirits are recited:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Daṃ liṅ liṃ yam vi ki ri ni mi ri ha sa na ra sa na ta ṭṭi sa na ṭṭi svāhā. [Seal Gesture.]
Interlace the two ring fingers inside each other and support them with the two thumbs;
extend the remaining four fingers apart, moving them back and forth.
The mantra for summoning the fifteen spirits is as follows:
Oṃ mīmogha-kāliśaye he ki puṣṭika aṅkuśe jaḥ hūṃ. [The mudrā is as follows: The hand gestures are as described.
Bend the five fingers of the right hand outward;
this is the method for summoning [the spirits] three times.
Next, when performing the rite of offering food (bali), the mantra for the fifteen spirits is recited while forming the vajra-pañjali mudrā.
Oṃ parāpudame ma le saṃbhave hūṃ. Next, the mantra for the fifteen *bhūta* spirits who consume satiated food is spoken:
Namo samantabuddhānāṃ. Oṃ hara hara yakṣaviniya dāni piñji piñji rāṭha gharalaṃ gharalaṃ hasana vihasana svāhā hūṃ vaṃ hūṃ. [The mudrā is as follows.]
The *vajra-añjali* is formed by pressing the tips of the two thumbs against the tips of the two index fingers; the commentary notes that this is the *vara-mudrā*.
Next, regarding the scattering of parched rice and flowers, it says: "Use the *vajra-pāṇi*."
Oṃ mahāmanibhūṣāya dara dara hūṃ hūṃ oṃ pravaravajravati sara sara hūṃ hūṃ. On the first, eighth, and fifteenth days of the waxing moon.
Under the constellation Jyeṣṭhā,
prepare various kinds of food, drink, fruits, and sweet milk-gruel— these six types of delicious offerings— and bestow them as gifts upon the divine kings.
May such deities cause all sentient beings to constantly afflict and harm those who harbor anger toward living beings and kill the myriad classes of people.
All illnesses of all sentient beings are caused by these spirit-kings.
Therefore, these fifteen spirit-kings always cherish those who recite the dhāraṇī spoken by me; such persons shall attain inexhaustible life.
All the celestial kings provide protection;
all the spirit-kings constantly bestow their guardianship.
By means of the sandalwood gandharvas...
Among all the great spirits in Jambudvīpa,
he is the most honored, the most supreme, and unsurpassed.
Write down the names of these ghost kings,
as well as the dhāraṇīs from within the sūtra,
using five-colored threads.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times; or twenty-one times;
or again, seven times.
Tie it around the neck.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one writes the name of the great spirit Candana-Gandharva on the forehead of a child.
Moreover, there is a method for those who suffer from worldly epidemics.
Using wood that subdues demons,
recite the mantra twenty-one times and have the patient drink it.
Furthermore, for those with eye diseases,
one should recite the mantra over flower-water twenty-one times;
they should then drink it and wash with it.
Furthermore, for one who has a chest ailment,
one should recite the mantra over a stone one hundred and eight times and have them drink it.
Furthermore, there is a method for treating ailments of the bowels.
If one suffers from jaundice or dysentery,
take *nugongcao* (Equisetum debile) and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times.
Drink it every day. Furthermore, for one suffering from the disease of malarial fever (yakṣman), there is a method:
recite the mantra over a large head [of grain] and drink it.
The illness will then be extinguished.
Furthermore, for one who has a disease of the head,
use a board made of willow wood.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times and place it beneath the head. Furthermore,
there is another method for those who wish to subdue wicked people.
Write down that person's name;
then, giving rise to a mind of anger and malice,
shoot that person’s name with an arrow from a bow once.
If one recites the aforementioned mantras for the fifteen spirits while calling out their names,
death will occur within three days.
At that time, all species of birds and all manner of monsters will gather together.
First, one should perform the ritual for malevolent spirits and recite the mantra over the object.
That which was created as a malevolent spirit will itself become possessed by a malevolent spirit and naturally perish.
Although there are many texts containing the fundamental collections of the Dharma,
they have not been fully recorded or compiled here;
this concludes the preceding commentary.
This Dharma extinguishes all evils and accomplishes all virtues;
it causes all that is sought to be fulfilled,
as well as all mundane and supramundane merit.
All high positions and all objects of affection will bring great good fortune.
In the *Kumāra-sūtra*’s method for recitation, there is the syllable "A" upon the maṇḍala;
this syllable transforms into a pavilion made of the seven precious jewels,
with a celestial canopy spread above the pavilion.
Adorned with various jewels,
within his palace there is a lotus-leaf seat, upon which is the syllable *Bhraṃ*.
This transforms into the Great Brahmā Deva King.
On the lotus leaf seat beside the King is the syllable *Śa*,
which transforms into the Great Gandharva King Candana.
On the edge of that lotus leaf is the syllable *Hūṃ*.
He became the leader of fifteen kings of ghosts and spirits,
surrounded before and behind by seventy-eight thousand deities and spirits.
On the eighth day of the eighth month of the first year of the Ping-chih era.
To arise; to flourish.
